text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The National Electoral Commission estimates about 8.9 million people registered as voters for this year's general elections.
- Two thousand students at Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology riot over a proposed bill on higher education which proposes to expel students failing to pay fees.
- The opposition FORD-Asili party pleads with other opposition parties to join in a campaign to disrupt presidential and parliamentary elections if minimum constitutional reforms are not made.

- Opposition National Democratic Party (NDP) founder member Stephen Omondi Oludhe declares himself party chairman and says he has sacked incumbent chairman Raila Odinga for his militant and uncompromising attitude.
- President Daniel arap Moi asks Kenyans to keep away from pro-reform rallies scheduled for July 7 across the country.
- Kenya Breweries staff on strike on Wednesday shouting "No reform, No Beer" are expected to resume work on Thursday.
- Energy Minister Kirugi M'Mukindia says the government is in the process of instituting legislation to reintroduce the regulation of oil prices.
- Opposition parliamentarian George Nyanja escapes a bid to arrest him outside parliament. ($1=54.50 Kenyan Shillings)
